WATER CONSERVATION BEHAVIOURAL INTENTIONS IN SIKKIM, INDIA: A STRUCTURAL EQUATION MODELING APPROACH

Journal: Water Conservation and Management (WCM)
Author: Aditya Rai, Sumeet Agarwal, Suditya Sapcotta, Jampala Maheshchandra Babu, Tina Shivnani
Print ISSN : 2523-5664

ABSTRACT

Water scarcity is an inevitable problem of the future, and the subtropical Himalayan region, Sikkim, the 22nd State of India, represents a paradoxical crisis. The reasons pertain to global warming due to rapid urbanisation, as well as behavioural waste and infrastructure constraints. This paper extends the Theory of Planned Behaviour (TPB) to predict water conservation intentions among a selected sample of 392 inhabitants residing in Sikkim. Structural equation modelling (SEM) has been used as an analytical tool. The findings of the study reveal perceived behavioural control (PBC) as the dominant predictor of behavioural intentions, with a β of 0.65 (p < 0.001), explaining 65% of the intention variance. The second predictor is subjective norms (SN), followed by attitude (AT), with SN: β = 0.20, p < 0.01; AT: β = 0.10, p < 0.05. The scores of SN-PBC; r=0.79; p < 0.001, were robust for the inter-construct correlations, and the model was within the metrics of acceptable validity where Cronbach’s α = 0.611–0.866; CR = 0.401–0.860; AVE = 0.401–0.558. PBC effects were found to be stronger in rural areas (β = 0.72) than in urban areas (β = 0.59). The findings of this paper challenge models that are purely attitudinal and, at the same time, highlight the importance of resource access interventions, given the Himalayan cultures’ collectivist orientation. This study contributes an extended, context-specific extension of TPB that covers understudied areas of the Himalayan subtropical lands. The research also focuses on the implications of policies based on perceived behavioural control strategies, norm-based campaigns, region-specific education, and infrastructure subsidies.
